role: six nonzero-baseline component fixtures with locked half-hours; no historical controller pilot
registration_context: zero-baseline component replays complete: four physically feasible, two service successes and two retained service failures; nonzero-baseline fixture outcomes not evaluated

information_and_time.clock: minute zero precedes request observation; own inventory and two previously locked baseline half-hours are known
information_and_time.baseline_lead: retain the one-hour baseline lead through immutable current and following half-hour inputs; do not renegotiate them
information_and_time.declaration: compute sustainable signed availability before the proposal, using the entire known 60-minute commitment path
information_and_time.execution: an issued BOA starts at minute zero, ramps for one minute from current PN to its absolute peak, holds 30 minutes, returns in one minute to the PN at minute 32; the remaining locked baseline then resumes
information_and_time.no_instruction: request=null executes the original baseline, whereas a zero-MW BOA overrides it during the pulse
information_and_time.future_receipts: none admitted as planning inputs; no realized price, historical publication-vintage limits or measured plant SOC used

service_and_physics: Keep 49 MW per-unit service capacity fixed as an analyst fixture obligation, not a historical converter rating or measured reserve contract
For nonzero PN distinguish service headroom/footroom from absolute MEL/MIL and BOA endpoints; service capacity must be sustainable relative to the known baseline throughout the offered hold
Constrain total absolute unit power and independent inventory continuously, including zero-crossing extrema, the PN change at minute 30 and the locked tail after minute 32
Both requested and admitted profiles are absolute MW; do not add a historical absolute BOA to PN
Retain availability shortfall separately from gross directional request shortfall; reducing declarations, partial dispatch or absent activation cannot waive the fixed availability obligation
An unsafe no-activation baseline is a known commitment failure; do not hide it by assuming a rescuing future request or altering the locked plan
Any admission/rationing rule is a simulation assumption, not an identified market response; physical feasibility and service success remain separate
fixture_basis: explicit component cases, not field histories; +/-13 MW exercise a nonzero changing baseline, 49 MW obligations are retained, and stock scenarios match the prior preflight
deliverable: extend the minimal contract, check independent physical traces and retain every service or commitment failure; report only six fixture results
decision: repair any physics or service-accounting discrepancy before integration; after component validation define already received BOA commitments and register a bounded causal pilot before reading its outcomes; no library matrix or source promotion on fixture completion
